 “Saturday Night Live” has set its next round of Season 52 hosts.
 As previously reported, Druski will headline the Nov. 7 episode — the first-ever digital content creator to headline the late-night sketch series. His episode comes ahead of the December release of his scripted Netflix series “Collect and Praise.” “ SNL ” has newly announced that Druski will be joined by the Strokes, marking the band’s fifth time serving as musical guest. They are currently on tour promoting their album “Reality Awaits.”

 Additionally, John Mulaney will host the Nov. 14 episode. This marks the comedian’s seventh time hosting “SNL” — on which he served as a writer for four seasons from 2008 to 2012. Though he’s still far from beating Alec Baldwin’s record of 17 hosting stints, he is one of the show’s most frequent hosts of all time. Mulaney appears in the upcoming Amazon Prime Video film “Madden” and is currently on a stand-up comedy tour titled “Mister Whatever.”
 Phoebe Bridgers will perform during Mulaney’s episode, marking her third time as musical guest after making her “SNL” debut in 2021 and returning alongside Boygenius collaborators Lucy Dacus and Julien Baker. She is currently on tour promoting her recent album “Lost Weekend.”
 As previously announced, this year’s Halloween episode will be headlined by “Obsession” star Inde Navarette and Gracie Abrams.
 Season 52 of “SNL” premiered on Sept. 26 with the New York Knicks’ Jalen Brunson as host and K-Pop group Katseye as musical guest. Dakota Johnson hosted the next episode — which featured a cameo from Taylor Swift — joined by Turnstile. On Oct. 10, Shane Gillis hosted “SNL” for the third time, performing a monologue that instantly became controversial for a joke in which he said that women “dress like whores” at the gym. He also dropped an f-bomb during a sketch.
